summary: Justified inference snippet extract for SOC audit: scoped redaction and ephemeral access
description:
Issue summary: SOC (internal security operations) has requested a small, justified extract of production inference request/response snippets to investigate a customer-reported escalation around suspected data leakage to an internal partner. This ticket requests approval and an operational runbook for producing a minimal, redacted snapshot of affected sessions and providing time-limited access to the SOC auditor group.

Impact: Low-likelihood but high-sensitivity. The extract will include potentially sensitive tokens from customer inputs and model outputs; improper handling risks PII exposure and compliance escalation. Extraction must be narrow, logged, and redacted according to our privacy rules.

Environment: prod (us-east-1) — narrow time window: 2026-03-02 00:00 → 2026-03-03 23:59 UTC.

Request details:
- Who requested: SOC (Emily Hart) via #soc-audit Slack thread and security@redwood-inference internal mailbox.
- Purpose: internal forensic review and proof for a regulatory inquiry related to a single customer's claim.
- Scope: up to 150 session IDs matching the saved search: "customer_company: AcmeCorp AND inference_time:[2026-03-02 TO 2026-03-03] AND similarity_score>0.85" (saved search created by SRE).
- Data to extract: for each session, include request metadata (timestamp, model version, route, request_id), and the first 3 user messages + first 3 assistant messages only.

Redaction plan (required):
1) Apply automated PII redaction pass that masks: email addresses, phone numbers, credit card patterns, SSNs, and 2+ token sequences matching customer-owned identifiers (customer_id, account numbers) with the token "[REDACTED]".
2) Remove full KV-cache dumps, attachments, and raw files — only keep inline text fields.
3) For any extracted model output that contains potential code execution or credential-like strings, replace with "[SANITIZED_CREDENTIAL]" and attach a redaction note.
4) Maintain an unredacted extract only in an encrypted ephemeral S3 object encrypted with a one-time KMS key and accessible to Security Engineers for 72 hours; reviewers must sign the access log.

Access method and controls:
- Extraction to be performed by SRE on-call (Diego Martinez) using the approved runbook commandset (not direct DB queries).
- Output location: ephemeral s3://redwood-internal-soc-audit/INT-19602/ with server-side encryption and object TTL 72h.
- IAM: grant read-only to group "soc-audit-reviewers" and require MFA + Just-In-Time approval from Security Manager (Emily Hart) before the KMS key can be used.
- Audit: all object downloads will be logged to CloudTrail and our internal access log (immutable). A copy of logs will be attached to the ticket.

Retention and deletion:
- The redacted copy (PII masked) will be stored in a workspace bucket for 30 days for follow-up; the unredacted copy will be destroyed after 72 hours.
- Deletion will be performed by SRE and logged; Legal will be notified when deletion is complete.

Justification & approvals required:
- Business justification provided by SOC: regulatory escalation tied to account AcmeCorp (support case SUP-94112).
- Approvals required: Security Manager (Emily Hart), Privacy Officer (Anika Rao), and SRE manager (Marcus Lee).

Acceptance criteria:
- Extraction limited to the saved search and capped at 150 sessions.
- Automated redaction run with sample validation (SRE to redact 10 random sessions and Security/Privacy to confirm).
- Logs and KMS use recorded and attached.
- Delivery: link to redacted s3 folder and confirmation of unredacted deletion.

Operational notes / runbook pointer: see Confluence: Data-Access-Approval-Checklist -> subsection "Forensic snippet extracts" for command examples and redaction script versions.

Required deliverables:
- Pre-extract sample: 3 fully-redacted sample sessions for Privacy approval.
- Full redacted bundle (tar.gz) + access log.
- Post-deletion verification report.

Timeline requested by SOC: extraction requested within 48 hours of ticket creation.
